record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README are present; source code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README says it reproduces the single-direction refusal intervention and reports results from applying it to Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct.
record.gate_note: The README reports intervention results for a layer sweep and a held-out evaluation. The separation scores and direction-similarity discussion are used to describe or select directions and are not recorded as rows. The README says capability benchmarks are not implemented.
record.test_reason: It reproduces the Arditi et al. difference-in-means direction and directional ablation on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct. It reports harmful refusal rates on 64 held-out prompts before and after a weight-orthogonalized edit.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The README presents the single direction as a strong approximation. It reports that removing the layer-21 direction cuts held-out harmful refusals from 100% to about 5% (4.7%), with harmless KL of 0.089. It cautions that some refusal can remain, edits can harm unrelated capabilities, and keyword-based evaluation is approximate. It says capability benchmarks and other models are not yet measured.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes this as a reproduction and implements difference-of-means directions, but records activations at the last prompt token, searches for a layer, and removes the selected direction through residual-writer hooks or weight orthogonalization. This is a research toolkit repository; the code was not read or run.
record.method_sensitivity: The removal outcome varies by layer: layers 1–12 leave refusal rates at 81–100%, layers 14–16 and 20–27 report 0%, and layers 13 and 17–19 report intermediate rates. KL also varies by layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful and harmless projections separate from about layer 14 (Cohen's d about 4 at layer 13, 9.5 by layer 19). Directions from layers 14–27 are mutually similar. The best-separating layer (26) is not the best layer to ablate (21).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction forms in mid layers and persists. Detectability and removability peak at different layers.

record.problems: One model and a small held-out set (64 harmful and 64 harmless prompts) are reported. Refusal detection is by keyword and is described as approximate; the README says capability benchmarks are not implemented. No uncertainty estimates or null-direction controls are reported. The README's stated clone URL uses refusal-prob while the repository ID is refusal-lens.
record.rows_left_out: No reported intervention outcomes omitted. Layer separation scores and direction-similarity values were left out because the README uses them to characterize or select directions rather than report intervention outcomes.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal. Retention of general capabilities: no benchmark is implemented, and KL alone is not interpretable. Only one model is tested.
The exported GGUF/Ollama model is not itself evaluated. Only one model, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct. No capability-retention measure.
Not tested. The README's remark that 'Refusal is not only one direction' is a general caveat, not a result.

record.verdict_notes: The layer-sweep rows (r1–r14) are selection values from 16+16 train prompts and should not carry verdicts. The reader's V4 'supports' label rested only on the 4.7% residual and a README caveat, so it is dropped. The reader's limits_scope labels were dropped because capability retention is untested, not shown to fail, and the residual refusals are within detector noise. Single model, n=64 per class, no uncertainty estimates, no random-direction control. The repository ID is refusal-lens but the clone and CI URLs say refusal-prob. This is a GitHub README, not peer reviewed.

versions.untested_parts: The README tests removal, not adding the direction. It does not establish that general capabilities are largely retained; KL is reported as a behavioral-change proxy, and the capability benchmark is not implemented.
Only one model is evaluated. The README reports an orthogonalized edited model but does not report evaluation of the exported GGUF itself.
No jailbreak attack or training against ablation is tested.
The README reports residual refusals after ablation and describes the single-direction account as an approximation, but does not test affine or cone geometries.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal-decision representation is tested.
No language or model-variant transfer is tested.
No comparison of refusal training methods or stages is tested.

relation.reason: Its own held-out results (100% -> 4.7% harmful refusal after the edit) bear directly on whether ablating or weight-editing the direction removes refusal.

tranche.reason: Same method and measure as Arditi et al.: a difference-of-means direction (128+128 train prompts), directional ablation turned into weight orthogonalization of embedding, attn o_proj and MLP down_proj, and refusal scored by substring matching. Small differences (last prompt token only, layer picked by lowest train refusal rate then KL, no Llama Guard) are recorded in the recipe and don't change the tranche.

source_check.notes: The results come from one seed and one model, use a keyword detector only (base harmless false positives 9.4%), give no uncertainty, have no random-direction control and measure no capabilities. The layer sweep on 16+16 train prompts (layers 1-12: 81-100%, 17-19: 13-19% refusal) is a selection result, not a held-out result. The README's git URL is fahd04/refusal-prob, not refusal-lens.
